work.text: A YouTube video that satisfies a brand brief, on a channel in the YouTube Partner Program, plus an OAuth token the miner serves so validators can read the channel's analytics. This repository is mechanism 0, the YouTube side, at about 2 percent of emission; the X side, mechanism 1, lives in a second repository and takes about 98 percent.
work.quote: Creators (miners) publish YouTube videos satisfying brand briefs; validators verify engagement via the YouTube Analytics API, score videos in USD terms
work.disagrees: The chain identity names only this repository and the explainer treats YouTube as the subnet's work; the README fetched 2026-09-19 says this code is mechanism 0 at about 2 percent of emission, with mechanism 1 for X at 98 percent in bitcast-network/bitcast-x.

scoring.text: A language model passes or fails the transcript against the brief. A passing video's score is the growth of its YouTube Premium partner revenue along a dampened square-root curve between two 7-day windows lagged 3 days, over its first 14 days, times a dollar factor by format (1800 dedicated, 400 ad read, 200 product placement) after a lifetime deduction of $100, $25 or $6.25. Non-Partner channels score zero.
scoring.quote: Dampened square-root curve: sqrt(v) / (1 + d*sqrt(v)); 0 for non-positive input.

split.text: Proportional to dollar-valued scores summed across briefs, folded into each validator's exponential moving average. Whatever the miners' weights do not add up to goes to burn uid 0, so emission tracks earned dollars rather than filling to 100 percent; with no active briefs everything burns. A treasury uid 106 exists in the constants with its share set to 0.0.
split.quote: Sum each miner's weights across briefs; the burn UID absorbs the remainder to 1.0.

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, against five miners. Commit-reveal is on. A validator does the reading itself: it pulls revenue and engagement from the YouTube Analytics API through the miner's token, calls a language model on Chutes to match brief to transcript, runs a prompt-injection auditor, and publishes hashed ids. Consensus constants are frozen so every validator's arithmetic matches bit for bit.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9, active_miners 5

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. A full reward cycle runs every 240 validator steps of 60 seconds, about 4 hours, and weights are set once the last update is older than the epoch length. A video is scoreable for 14 days after release. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 50,400 blocks, seven days, ten times the usual 5,000.

buyer.text: Brands, none named. The dashboard on 2026-09-20 shows $438.1K lifetime revenue, $276.7K of it spent buying back the subnet token, and $539.5K paid to creators across YouTube and X. There is no brand-facing page, no price for a brief and no contact. The 2025 substack post addresses creators with a target CPM of $1,200 and names no client.

exploits.text: Bought or spiked traffic: a scoring period is capped at the channel's median daily value over days 60 to 30 before, so a sudden jump earns at most the usual rate; the 2025 post calls this the performance lookback. Only positive Partner Program revenue counts, watch time never substitutes, and stake no longer stands in for Partner status. Descriptions and transcripts are screened for prompt injection before the brief check.
exploits.quote: proportional scaling caps a scoring period at the channel's historical median
